title: Jacob’s impaired sight in old age
summary: Genesis associates Jacob’s impaired sight with old age. Modern eye science supports an increased risk of sight-threatening conditions with age, without making blindness inevitable.
text: KJV Genesis 48:10: “Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see.” The National Eye Institute describes an increased risk of eye diseases in older adults, while emphasizing that vision loss need not be a normal part of aging.
reasoning: The agreement concerns the specific association between older age and impaired sight. The source supports increased risk, not a diagnosis of Jacob or a claim that age alone necessarily causes blindness.
scope: The narrative provides no eye examination or clinical history sufficient to identify a disease, measure visual acuity or establish complete blindness. A literary emphasis on Jacob’s blessing and discernment can coexist with the reported impairment; science does not establish that reading. No original-language claim is made. The comparison does not verify Jacob’s reported age, reconstruct an event, assign a date or give a verdict on the whole passage.

sources.label: National Eye Institute, NIH · Vision and Aging Resources

fields.text: The National Eye Institute identifies cataract, glaucoma and age-related macular degeneration among conditions whose risk increases with age. These are examples of possible causes of impairment in older adults, not diagnoses of Jacob.
